A. Does recent evidence support the size of effect we assume: does this measure reduce deaths among the people it reaches, and by how much?
Measure: Low-dose CT screening for long-term heavy smokers. Invite 50-74-year-old long-term heavy smokers to low-dose CT with smoking cessation support, so cancers are found before symptoms. Finland is piloting this in 2026-2028.
effect_summary_en: Nine randomised trials pooled: lung cancer death rate ratio 0.84 (0.76–0.92), i.e. 16% fewer lung cancer deaths with LDCT screening.
supported_en: The Lancet Regional Health – Europe meta-analysis (2021) shows RR 0.84 (0.76–0.92) for lung cancer death across nine trials.
not_supported_en: The pages read don't show the baseline death rate of 3.30 per 1,000 person-years, or that people in a pilot people sign up for themselves would have the same risk as trial participants.
in_use_quote: Tammikuussa käynnistyy keuhkosyövän seulontapilotti, josta vastaavat Suomen Syöpärekisteri yhdessä Oulun yliopistollisen sairaalan kanssa.

in_use_source.title: OYS mukana keuhkosyövän seulontapilotissa - tavoitteena parantaa taudin varhaista toteamista - Pohde

in_use_summary_en: OYS and the Finnish Cancer Registry have run a two-year national research pilot since January 2026, open to self-enrolled 50–74-year-old long-term smokers from North Ostrobothnia; it is not a routine screening service.
summary_en: Pohde says a lung cancer screening pilot started in January 2026, run by the Finnish Cancer Registry together with OYS. It covers people aged 50–74 who have smoked for more than 25 years, including people from North Ostrobothnia. It is a two-year research study looking for 1,200 participants in five regions: only some of them get low-dose CT, everyone is offered help to stop smoking, and people sign up themselves. A 2021 meta-analysis of nine randomised trials in The Lancet Regional Health – Europe found 16% lower lung cancer mortality (RR 0.84, 95% CI 0.76–0.92), which matches the effect our model assumes.
unanswered_en: No page read says whether screening will continue as a routine programme after the pilot, or how many of the participants come from North Ostrobothnia.
